title: Ephesus, 431
hookLine: Mary is God-bearer; the Church of the East and Rome signed a shared statement on Christ in 1994
last: THE LORD AND GIVER OF LIFE.

cards: "And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?" That's Elizabeth in Luke's Gospel, greeting her cousin Mary at the door. The mother of my Lord.
Christians in the East came to call Mary by a Greek title, Theotokos, the God-bearer, the one who gave birth to God.
Then a bishop of Constantinople, Nestorius, objected: call her the mother of Christ, he said; don't say she bore God. It sounds like a quarrel about Mary. It was really a quarrel about her son.
The bishops who answered it met in a city called Ephesus.

teach.h: MOTHER OF GOD: A WORD ABOUT JESUS.
teach.b: The Catechism says the Council of Ephesus proclaimed in 431 that Mary truly became the Mother of God, by the human conception of the Son of God in her womb.

It was guarding against the idea that Christ was a human person joined to the divine person of God's Son, two someones sharing one body. Ephesus said no. The child Mary carried was not a man God later moved into.

He was God the Son, become man in her. So when Catholics call Mary Mother of God, they are first saying something about Jesus: the one she held in her arms is the one through whom all things were made.
It's the title in the Hail Mary: Holy Mary, Mother of God. The story has a second half.
One family of Christians, the Assyrian Church of the East, did not accept the council's decisions, and the two churches went separate ways.
Then in 1994 Pope John Paul II and the Catholicos-Patriarch of the Church of the East, Mar Dinkha the Fourth, signed a common statement on Christ.
In it they confess the same faith in Christ, truly God and truly man, one person.

They note that the Church of the East prays to Mary as the Mother of Christ our God and Savior, while the Catholic Church calls her the Mother of God and also the Mother of Christ, and each recognizes the other's words as expressing the same faith.
Not everything between them is settled. But on who Christ is, two churches found they had been saying the same thing in different words.

how: Catholics call Mary the Mother of God in the Hail Mary and keep the Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God on the first of January; the 1994 common declaration with the Assyrian Church of the East is part of the Church's ecumenical dialogue.

games.q: you're a bishop at Ephesus. some want Mary called only the mother of Christ, so as not to say she bore God. what do you say?
o: agree; leave God out of it.
call her Theotokos, because her son is one person, truly God.
stop speaking of Mary at all.
games.why: the council proclaimed Mary truly Mother of God, by the human conception of the Son of God in her womb.

practice: The Church of the East prays in an ancient Syriac tradition; hold its Christians in mind, even if you've never met one.
If you pray, pray for them and for the unity their leaders and the popes have been walking toward; if you don't, wish them peace.
If an old quarrel of your own turned out to be about words more than substance, let it sit beside them.

wordCard.voice: Ephesus. The council that called Mary Mother of God, Theotokos, to say that her son is one person, truly God. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: God-bearer, the title Ephesus upheld for Mary.
